naya.summary: Oscar review: v3 is a materially stronger foundation but not yet 10/10 because several enforcement and integration layers remain incomplete. The next elevation should move from documented architecture to mechanically enforced memory transactions, semantic retrieval, automated CIS generation, and feed receipts.
findings: Strong: event-centric chronological storage, paired representations, provenance, verification law, explicit history/conflict model, migration manifest, canonical index, model-independent bootstrap.
Gap 1: v3 validation/runtime is not yet executed in CI, so structural correctness is not continuously proven.
Gap 2: retrieval is currently lexical/alias based, not true semantic/vector/hybrid retrieval.
Gap 3: note write, index update, and receipt are separate repository writes; a crash between them can create partial state. A transactional/outbox pattern is needed.
Gap 4: verification receipts are stored, but product-feed posting is not mechanically integrated.
Gap 5: Daily Intelligence is currently synthesis logic, not an automated scheduled/triggered verified report pipeline.
Gap 6: duplicate detection is a rule/architecture requirement, not yet an implemented similarity service.
Gap 7: event IDs are timestamp-based; a ULID/UUID/content-hash component would strengthen distributed uniqueness and idempotency.
Gap 8: higher-order reports need explicit supersession/versioning and source coverage checks to prevent silent omissions.
recommended_elevation: Introduce an append-only event log plus derived indexes and an outbox for receipts/feed publication.
Use hybrid retrieval: time filters + lexical + aliases + embeddings + relationship traversal.
Add idempotency keys and deterministic event fingerprints for duplicate prevention.
Automate Daily/Weekly/Monthly CIS generation with source manifests and verification.
Add observability metrics: retrieval hit rate, duplicate rate, verification latency, orphan rate, report coverage, and stale-memory rate.

human.summary: Oscar says the new architecture is good enough to become the foundation, but it is not a finished superbrain yet. The biggest difference between an excellent design and a truly 10/10 system is enforcement: the machine needs to prove, automatically and continuously, that memory was saved correctly, indexed, retrievable, and reflected into CIS.
findings: The architecture is logical and scalable.
The next work is automation and enforcement, not another folder redesign.
human.recommendation: Keep this architecture. Harden the machinery around it instead of redesigning the core again.

evidence: Review was performed against the canonical v3 constitution, bootstrap, event index, migration manifest, runtime, and verified legacy-folder deletion.
